note: Build-speed budget for scripts/bench-build.sh --budget (the build-perf CI jobs and the nightly). RATIO FORM: before every repetition of every case the script times a fixed reference workload on the same machine (a cold `go build` of the Go std packages in `reference.packages`, empty GOCACHE), and each key's `wall_ratio` is the case's median wall time divided by that reference. A measured ratio above wall_ratio x factor fails, unless the wall is also within (wall_ratio x this run's reference) + slack_s, the absolute floor that keeps a sub-second build from failing on jitter. Peak RSS stays absolute (budget x factor, plus slack_bytes). Why: ubuntu-latest runners are not one machine. The same cold app50-web build took 30-47 s on different runners (ten parallel runs of one commit, bench-probe run 38899508863), an absolute 1.55x spread that failed build-perf on the slow runners (2 of 8 runs on main, 4 of 7 on ci/ubuntu-latest); as a ratio to the reference the same ten runs spread 1.05x for the cold build and at most 1.10x for any build above 2 s. The factor is therefore 1.25 (it was 1.5 against absolute seconds): a 25% slowdown of Sky on the same runner fails, whatever the runner. Proof: a real slowdown measured on CI (the same runs with GOFLAGS=-p=1 slowing every Sky go build but not the reference, bench-probe legs 11 and 12) raises the cold app50-web ratio from 3.96 to 5.12-5.17 and fails this budget, while the slow and fast runners of the normal legs pass; rust/crates/xtask/tests/build_budget_normalises_runner_speed.rs replays the rule on fixtures (a 1.6x slower runner passes, a 1.6x slower build fails on either runner). linux-x86_64 is the median over the bench-probe runs named in its `seeded_from` (app50 keys over 14 runs, the app100 and skyshop keys over 4 full-set runs; go 1.26, ubuntu-latest, 4 vCPU). darwin-arm64 keeps its 2026-10-15 walls (an Apple silicon Mac, 8 CPUs, 16 GB, go1.26.1, docs/perf/runs/build-speed-20261015/ci-shape.json) with ratios to the reference measured on the same machine and Go version on 2026-10-16 (median of 5 runs); it is a local comparison only, and the next local --write-budget re-seeds it in full. Re-seed a platform with: scripts/bench-build.sh --reps 3 --cases "app skyshop" --write-budget <file> on that platform (the nightly uploads build-budget.proposed.json), ideally the median of several runs.

linux-x86_64.seeded_from: build-perf-nightly build-budget.proposed.json of the six release-gate runs 42973337533, 43251373132, 43275758715, 43283866631, 43393493206, 43399491576 (v0.29.9 at c7c411f24 to 1fd2e6eda, 2026-11-11 to 2026-11-13); per key the median of the per-run values. Re-seeded because the Go runtime grew: non-test runtime-go went from about 128k lines at the 2b9e007a9 seed to about 181k at v0.29.9, every build links all of rt, and every key's ratio rose with it (app100-web:app/edit 1.63 -> 1.85). No single commit regressed; see the PR that re-seeded it.
